title: Sequences of events and sensor anomalies
request: Let DCLab alert before machine failures from streams of sensor readings, judged by the failures it catches, how early, and the alerts it costs.
spec: A kind for streams: windows over the stream, features from each window's past, labels that may be sparse or delayed; detectors from 15.5 applied per window and supervised models when labels exist; event-based metrics (detection delay, alerts per day, recall of incidents rather than of rows); splits by time and machine. Done when the replica (machines with planted failures and their warning signs) reports detection delay and incident recall, with no window using the future.
plan: Build windows from each unit's past only, with a change score against the unit's own level.
Label windows by incidents in the horizon after them; drop the downtime.
Fit methods early in the training period, set thresholds out of sample for an alert budget, choose there, read the holdout once.
Score by incident: caught in the horizon, lead time, alerts per unit-day; and on machines never seen.
Review, fix, and show each test fails on the fault it guards.

decisions.decision: The leak check recomputes the windows with every later reading changed, instead of reading a window's own bookkeeping.
decisions.why: The last-read time came from a backward match, so a centred rolling window that read 12 hours ahead still reported nothing read after the end.

decisions.decision: Thresholds are set on scores of rows the model never saw.
decisions.why: In-sample scores set the budget on the rows the model fitted; on new rows the isolation forest alerted 0.308 per machine-day against 0.2.

decisions.decision: An incident is scored only when its whole horizon lies in the scored period, and its horizon starts after the previous repair.
decisions.why: Incidents at the period's edge had their warning cut to 12 hours, and one alert credited two failures.

decisions.decision: The holdout line is set from the window ends alone.
decisions.why: Labelling drops windows in downtime, so the incidents themselves moved the line and every threshold with it.

change: dclab_core/streams.py, dclab_core/replicas/machine_sensors.py, dclab_rnd/kinds/streams.py, tests/test_core_streams.py, dclab_core/CHANGELOG.md, dclab_rnd/kinds/capability.json.

findings.defect: The check that no window reads past its end could never fail.
findings.scenario: A centred rolling window (12 hours of future) and a shifted feature both reported 0 readings after the end and passed every check.
findings.cause: The last-read time came from the matching step, not from what the features read.
findings.fix: A future check that recomputes the windows with later readings changed and counts the windows that moved.
findings.impact: A leaking stream model would have been recorded as clean.

findings.defect: Every unit's first window had a change score near 1e9.
findings.scenario: On seed 0 the 24 largest scores were each machine's first window; they took 24 of the 289 alerts the budget allowed.
findings.cause: A baseline of one reading has no spread.
findings.fix: A baseline needs a few windows of readings and a spread above a floor; otherwise no score.

findings.defect: The guard counted incidents the readings never matched.
findings.scenario: Five incidents for a unit with no readings passed; the classifier fitted one class and alerted on all 2538 holdout windows.
findings.fix: Incidents of the units present, in the fitting period, and both classes required.

findings.defect: Alert thresholds came from in-sample scores.
findings.scenario: The budget of 0.2 alerts per machine-day became 0.34 on unseen machines and 0.308 on validation for the forest.
findings.cause: Thresholds were set on the rows the model was fitted on.
findings.fix: Thresholds on the validation period, out of sample.

findings.defect: Incidents near a period's edge were scored with a cut-short horizon.
findings.scenario: A failure 18 hours into the holdout had 1 of its 8 warning windows in it, capping its lead time at 12 hours.
findings.cause: Bounds counted incidents whose horizon crossed the line.
findings.fix: Only incidents whose whole horizon lies in the scored period.

findings.defect: One alert credited every incident after it, and the replica planted failures during repairs.
findings.scenario: Two failures 17 hours apart on M00 shared their windows.
findings.cause: No floor at the previous repair; no spacing in the generator.
findings.fix: An incident's horizon starts after the previous repair; failures are spaced past warning and repair.

findings.defect: The unseen-machine evaluation was not split by time.
findings.scenario: The model trained on the other machines' whole history, after the held machines' windows; training on every unit passed.
findings.fix: Unseen machines use the same periods: fitted on the others' training period, read on their holdout period.

findings.scenario: Fitting on the holdout, nearest matching of step ends and a forward baseline all passed.
findings.cause: A perfect hourly grid with no gaps.
findings.fix: Gappy readings, a by-hand baseline, thresholds that the holdout's incidents cannot move, and the budget held on validation.

findings.defect: 15.5's detectors and delayed labels were missing, and detection delay was named lead time.
findings.scenario: Only an isolation forest and an own score ran; a label known three days late was used at once.
findings.fix: Detectors injected (percentile rules, ECOD); a label delay; the delay after onset stated as not measured.

findings.defect: The kind took over survival briefs.
findings.scenario: 'Survival analysis of machine failures … with censored machines' was detected as streams.

outcome: Built as a library and accepted on the replica (6 decisions); refused by the engine and partial in the matrix.
lessons: Prove a leak check can fail by planting a leak it must catch; bookkeeping of what was read is not proof.
Set thresholds on rows the model never saw, or the budget means nothing on new data.
Score an event only where its whole horizon is in the period.
Fix the holdout line before labelling, so the labels cannot move it.
risks: Alert budgets that hold only in sample.
Incidents counted twice or with cut horizons.
Labels used before they are known.
